outcome: REJECTED -- draft compiled and looked reasonable (mirrored the RecipeDetailBatchFixTests/FirstCookoutFeedBugBatchTests async-let double-tap pattern), but a RED-proof run revealed the technique itself is unsound here: CookJournalEntryView's `isSaving` lives in the View's own `@State`, and directly instantiating a View struct outside a live SwiftUI hierarchy does NOT give @State a persistent shared box -- a diagnostic (sequential, non-concurrent) call to `view.save()` showed `view.isSaving` reading back `false` immediately after the call returned, proving the mutation never round-trips to the caller's copy. The existing precedent for this technique (FirstCookoutFeedBugBatchTests) only works because it shares state via an external Binding<Set<Int>>, never the view's own @State. Deleted the test; shipped the source fix without automated coverage, matching the PR #754 precedent (ProfileEditView Return-key fix) which also shipped a View-layer @State fix with no new test for the same underlying reason.
